Before a key activates, the applicant publishes the challenge string in a DNS TXT record on a domain it controls. The node resolves it, then reads the registry: the site must be 730 days old and the registrant name must match the verified wallet. One registrant, one key.

The kernel of the cost is age. A fresh .com runs 11 dollars a year and no registrar backdates a creation date, so fifty clones wait two years or pay near 150 dollars for aged names, 7,500 in an afternoon.

Marble hardens under decades of pressure; a lagoon hides its channel beneath a flat surface.
